title: Rust engine parity: third audit and remaining gaps
summary: A third audit compared the Rust engine with the frozen JavaScript game and four pull requests (#299 to #302) fixed what it found: menu, focus and room-ended flows, following a host's course change, the JavaScript error wording, uniform randomness, the boot loading screen and startup error panel, music stream validation, the stinger bus, water failure handling, and ported JavaScript tests that exposed soundtrack bugs. All four are merged, and #297 from the previous entry has also merged. Production serves b1d2e44.
details: Menus, focus and room flows (#299): every menu now polls the controller at display rate and draws only on input change, with nothing drawn while idle. A failed ride load returns to the page it started from with the error shown: Freestyle to course select, Race to race setup, Free Ride to the main menu, a room to Multiplayer. This also fixed a panic already on main, where the first frame after any failed load hit a non-existent GPU resource. A room that closes for good ends the ride on Multiplayer (main for Free Ride) with the reason, a closed socket drops the other riders and their sounds at once, and Leave Game returns to the matching page. On the web, focus follows the window instead of the canvas, so focusing a Host/Join field or the install banner no longer pauses the ride, music or pad polling. Fullscreen keeps the DOM inputs and status line visible. Tab and Shift+Tab walk fields and choices, Back opens a page on its first row, P resumes only while bound to Pause, and a Freestyle ride is the only thing that changes the saved Freestyle course. The touch flip cue, flip-zone arcs and Arcade spin arcs now draw.

Host course changes and error wording (#300): when the host changes course while a guest is in the garage or course picker, the guest now goes straight to the new course's loader and rides from the start line with the garage's current ATV, as the JavaScript follow does. The failed-load notice now uses the JavaScript wording: the browser's own message for a refused request (Failed to fetch), Original content package is unavailable (N), Original game content could not load (N), Hosted content integrity check failed, the content manifest validation messages and the missing-archive and missing-member messages. Lobby errors read Unable to connect to this lobby and Connection lost (N). The ride behind Change ATV and Select Track was checked and already matched: the frontend covers it, its sound is muted and the menu tune plays; the relay test now asserts the tune.

Randomness (#301): the engine now has one uniform source where the JavaScript used Math.random: the browser's on the web, an OS-seeded generator on desktop. The clock digits it replaces were skewed. Rain odds used a sample stuck in the upper half, so NAT06 rained about 80% instead of 90% and SX13 about 60% instead of 80%. The race intro stinger was always INT001, and loading tips only ever showed 7 of the 14 tips. The CPU roster seed, the Rider NNNN name, the soundtrack session seed and the shared-room meet order use it too.

Boot, music and water (#301): the web page shows the Now Loading panel with the brand, Preparing menus and a sweeping meter until the Rust frontend draws, fitting 390x844, 844x390 and 667x375. A startup failure closes the loader and shows the error on the menu notice panel instead of the monospace status strip. Music stream records are rejected unless they are a music VAG record, audio/mp4, within 25 MiB, with a lowercase sha256, the matching /content url and positive seconds, with the content.js test cases ported. The IntOut stingers have their own mixer bus at the music volume, past the Alpha muffle and the Jukebox analyser, as in audio.js. Invalid water data now fails the ride load with its error, while a restored context keeps riding without the surface. Jukebox seek and length use the manifest's seconds, clamped to length minus 0.25 s.

Ported JavaScript tests and the bugs they found (#302): new tests cover gamepad selection (Auto follows the pad in use, resting devices never take over, a pinned pad wins), keyboard help labels, ride audio (train loop markers, rain voice through Reset and pause, rider impact guard), weather per venue with the random source pinned, soundtrack behaviour, page lifecycle, wake lock retry and touch utilities. They exposed real fixes: Music Off stopped the song so Music On started another, and it now pauses in place and resumes the same song. A failed song read turned Music off on desktop or ended the web VAG fallback for the session, and now only stops reads until the next choice. On the web VAG fallback a Jukebox choice kept playing the old song. Sound that became ready after a skipped race intro lost the intro's hold and stinger. Gamepad baselines are now taken for every pad at first sight, also while another pad is pinned.

Verification: host-only. Each PR ran cargo fmt, clippy with warnings denied and the touched crates' unit tests, with a wasm build or wasm clippy where the web engine changed. #299 ran 18 focused content tests and all 11 relay tests including native-host cases; #300 ran 4 content tests and 6 local-relay tests; #301 ran the boot, race, alpha muffle, jukebox and shell browser tests; #302 ran 15 content browser tests on host Chromium, with WebKit for touch.
limitation: All checks are host-only (headless Chromium, with WebKit for touch); nothing was verified on a physical phone. Windows and Linux desktop were not run and no desktop release was built. play.html is still the JavaScript game until the user switches it (draft #284). Known gaps from the PR bodies: the touch visuals are checked by display-list unit tests, not compared on screen with play.html; the content loader shares one request per chunk only for prefetched requests, unlike content.js; desktop keeps its own wording for local file and pack errors; a manifest that is not valid JSON still shows serde's message instead of the browser's SyntaxError text; #300 had no negative control run against a build without the fix; #297 has no browser test with a rider beyond 864 ft and its speed-rush and vegetation changes were not compared visually; and the JavaScript 'Next uses the audible song when the next track is buffered' test has no Rust counterpart.
